Prevention: Select seedlings free from scale insects.
Follow regular removal and destruction of infested branches, fallen leaves and fruits by burning or burying at least 30 cm deep.
Apply recommended doses of manure and fertilizer as well as irrigation schedules to keep the plants healthy.
Monitoring: Monitor field weekly to check for the presence of scale on five randomly selected green twigs and 5-10 leaves per twig and five randomly selected fruit per tree.
Observe honeydew (a sugary substance) secreted by scales.
Black coloured sooty mould (a fungus) grows on the honeydew coating leaves, twigs and fruit.
Observe the defoliation of trees and dead twigs for the presence of scales.
Action threshold : 1-3+ red scale on 10% or > fruits, soft brown scale 15%, Cottony
Scales are highly active from spring to autumn and less active in winter.
Direct Control: Conserve natural predators such as ladybirds and
Green lacewings by planting attractive flowering plants on the ridge or border of orchard.
Spray petroleum (horticultural) oil @ 10 ml per litre water. (Generally 3 times (April, August/ September and
November/ December; The decision to spray should depend on real need and on the monitoring results).

Note : 3-5 litre of water suspension/solution is required per citrus pant.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment (PPE) while using chemical pesticides.
Pesticides are harmful to natural enemies, do not spray more than label recommendation.
Oil sprays can be toxic to trees, particularly applied when trees are water stressed in hot weather.
Besides, take care of natural enemies while spraying chemical insecticides.
